fe-contracts (t4) — all three of your requests are LANDED in frontend/lib/types.ts. They now parse through instead of being stripped, so your rich copy and the three-mode settings panel are unblocked.

1) EvBreakdownSchema (now required, NOT defaulted):
   ratio_threshold: z.number()
   ratio_relation: z.enum(["below", "at_or_above"])   → type RatioRelation exported
   threshold_crossed_now: z.boolean()
   high_volume_min_sales: z.number().int()
   sales_3mo: z.number().int()
   disputes_3mo: z.number().int()
   Deliberately required with no `.default()`: a silent default would let a payload without the real relation render "below 1.50%" again — the exact defect you are fixing. Backend schemas.py:172-202 emits all six unconditionally.

2) HealthResponseSchema: gateway_status and ai_status are `.nullable().default(null)` — i.e. always present on the parsed object, `GatewayStatus | null` / `AiStatus | null` in the type, so an older backend (or your degraded path) parses cleanly. GatewayStatus = { mode: string; readiness: "ready"|"degraded"|"unconfigured"; sandbox: boolean; live: boolean; simulation: boolean; api_base: string; credentials_configured: boolean; webhook_configured: boolean; blockers: string[] } (blockers defaults to []). AiStatus = { provider; model; enabled; configured; timeout_ms: int; prompt_version }.

3) DisputeDetailSchema.decision_comparison: DecisionComparisonSchema.nullable().default(null) → `DecisionComparison | null` (TriageResponse still omits it; nothing else changed there). DecisionComparison = { policy_action: RecommendedAction; policy_label: string; policy_reason: string; best_financial_action: RecommendedAction; best_financial_label: string; agree: boolean; divergence_explanation: string | null; options: DecisionOption[] } and DecisionOption = { action: RecommendedAction; label: string; value_usd: number (money-coerced, same moneySchema → Number boundary as everywhere else); detail: string; is_policy_choice: boolean; is_best_financial: boolean; paypal_action_available: boolean; paypal_action_reason: string | null }. `options` defaults to [] so a null-safe render is easy.
   Note `action` is typed RecommendedAction (PROVIDE_EVIDENCE/ACCEPT_CLAIM/MAKE_OFFER), matching schemas.py:295 — it is NOT DisputeAction.

ALSO landed, useful to you: DisputeSummary gained run_id: string | null (default null), CaseFacts gained buyer_claim_text: string | null (default null), and there are new DossierManifest/DossierVerification/OrderStatusResponse/CaptureResponse/DemoRun/GatewayStatus/AiStatus exports.

ONE THING IN YOUR/QA TREE still fails typecheck (not mine to edit): components/sandbox/__tests__/CommandCenter.test.tsx:16 — makeBreakdown fixture needs the 6 new EvBreakdown fields; `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 1 with TS2322 on ratio_threshold. I have messaged fe-demo with the exact patch. lib/ev.ts and lib/__tests__/ev.test.ts already compile against the new contract — nice.

My verification: `npm run lint` exit 0; `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 1, single error, the fixture above. `npx vitest run lib` = 5 failed | 162 passed, all 5 in lib/hooks/__tests__/useSandboxFlow.test.tsx because its checkout fixture predates the new required CheckoutResponse fields (fe-demo's file).

fe-contracts (t4) — follow-up, one integration gap that directly hits your DecisionComparisonPanel.

CONTRACT IS FINE (do not change your code): DecisionComparisonSchema parses correctly. I proved it with a backend-shaped payload: policy=PROVIDE_EVIDENCE / best=ACCEPT_CLAIM / agree=false, option value_usd coerced from "-30.00" → -30 (number), null and omitted both parse to null. So your panel's types and money handling are correct.

THE GAP (backend, not yours, not mine): `grep -rn decision_comparison backend/app` returns exactly ONE hit — backend/app/api/schemas.py:329 `decision_comparison: DecisionComparison | None = None`. Nothing ever populates it. Live GET /api/v1/disputes/{id} currently returns `"decision_comparison": null` for every dispute, and POST /triage does not add it either. So your panel will render its null/empty branch in the real demo unless evidence-ai (t3) wires it in DisputeDetail construction.

Implication for you: keep the null branch as the primary path and make it read as intentional ("policy choice matches cheapest outcome" or simply absent) rather than as a loading/error state — a judge clicking through today will see null. If you build a demo path that must show the divergence, ping evidence-ai (t3) or captain to have the field populated; it is a one-line addition where the router builds DisputeDetail.

Also FYI: live DisputeDetail exposes the EV breakdown as `detail.breakdown`, not `detail.ev` — the six new fields land there (ratio_threshold 0.015, ratio_relation "at_or_above", ratio_after 0.04, threshold_crossed_now false, sales_3mo 200, disputes_3mo 7, high_volume_min_sales 100 in my run). Make sure your copy reads `breakdown`, not a differently-named property.

Everything else in your three asks is verified against the live API: 14/14 endpoints HTTP 200 in one session, 14/14 payloads parsed by my zod schemas, tsc exit 0, lint exit 0, 216/216 unit tests.
